_about: How the archive's readable copy renders an amount, and the only data it needs to do it. contract/DATA-CONTRACT.md 8.2 and 8.5, issue #331.
_why: The readable copy used to ask java.text.NumberFormat, which is backed by Android's bundled ICU on the phone and by the JDK's CLDR of a different vintage anywhere else. The same call, the same locale tag and the same currency produced Latin digits on one and Arabic-Indic on the other, so 8.5's byte identical regeneration could hold on one phone and fail on any second reader of this contract. /contract exists because there are meant to be two readers. So money is formatted here, from this file, by rules a reader can implement in an afternoon, exactly as ReadableDate spells month names itself rather than asking the locale.
_rules: The amount is stored as an integer number of minor units and is never converted to a floating point number at any point.
The number of minor units in one major unit is 10 raised to the exponent below. The exponent for a code not listed is 2.

Digits are the Latin digits 0 to 9, always, in every language. This is the same deliberate exception ReadableDate makes for month names: the stranger this document must survive is a records office or a lawyer, and a figure that is unreadable to them is worse than a figure that is not in their conventional digits.

The integer part is grouped in threes from the right, separated by a comma. The fractional part is separated by a period and is always exactly as many digits as the exponent, including trailing zeros, because 5.00 and 5.0 and 5 are three different statements about a bill.
A negative amount carries a leading minus sign before everything else.

The ISO 4217 code follows the amount after one ordinary space. The code rather than a symbol, because $ is at least six different currencies and a symbol is exactly the ambiguity this whole section exists to remove.
An exponent of 0 renders no separator and no fractional part at all.
_exponents_note: Only the codes whose exponent is not 2, from ISO 4217. Everything else is 2, which is the overwhelming majority and is the default rather than a list nobody can audit. A code this file has never heard of renders with 2, which is the right guess and is stated rather than silent.
